# Evolution of NLP Applications in Finance

## Historical Development

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="100%"}
- **Traditional rule-based approaches (1960s – 1990s)** keyword spotting and hand-written grammars for parsing bank statements and wire stories. Access to computing power limited to large institutions.
- **Statistical methods (1990s – 2010s)** – TF-IDF, n-grams, naïve Bayes sentiment. 
- **Machine-learning era (2010s)** – supervised classifiers & finance-specific dictionaries.  
- **Deep-learning revolution (≈2015 +)** – word-embeddings, CNN/RNN sentiment on earnings calls, topic models.
- **Large Language Models (2018 +)** – GPT-style chatbots & summarizers now embedded in research and advisory workflows (see Morgan Stanley GPT-4 Assistant 2023).
:::

::::

---

## Selected Academic Milestones (2004 – 2024)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
- **Antweiler & Frank 2004, *JF*** – Internet-forum sentiment & volatility  
- **Tetlock 2007, *JF*** – WSJ pessimism predicts next-day returns  
- **Dougal *et al.* 2012, *RFS*** – Columnist-specific tone moves the market  
- **Loughran & McDonald 2011, *JF*** – Finance-specific tone dictionaries for 10-Ks  
- **Jegadeesh & Wu 2013, *JFE*** – Market-reaction-weighted tone metric  
- **Chen *et al.* 2014, *RFS*** – Seeking Alpha opinions predict returns & EPS surprises  
- **Manela & Moreira 2017, *JFE*** – NVIX text-based disaster-risk index  
- **Buehlmaier & Whited 2018, *RFS*** – Text-identified financial-constraints premium  
- **Hassan *et al.* 2019, *QJE*** – Firm-level political-risk from earnings-call text  
- **Bybee *et al.* 2024, *JF*** – Topic-model news-attention indices improve macro forecasts
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
**Why it matters**

- Predict **returns**, **volatility**, and **risk premia**  
- Reveal intangible firm traits (constraints, political risk)  
- Enhance macro forecasting with text-derived factors  
- Methodology shifted: word-counts → ML classification → embeddings & topic models
:::

::::

---

## Real-World Industry Applications of NLP

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
- **Thomson Reuters / Bloomberg News Analytics** – Real-time machine-readable sentiment feeds power quant desks and HFT strategies  
- **RavenPack** – >70 % of top quant funds ingest its news-sentiment data for alpha & risk  
- **MarketPsych Capital (2008-10)** – Hedge fund trading on media sentiment, +28 % during the 2008 crisis  
- **Derwent Capital "Twitter Fund" 2011** – $40 m portfolio guided by Twitter mood  
- **J.P. Morgan COIN 2017** – NLP reviews loan contracts in seconds, saving 360 k lawyer-hours  
- **Morgan Stanley GPT-4 Assistant 2023-24** – Chatbot for 16 k advisors, instant Q&A on 100 k research docs  
- **Kensho (acq. S&P Global 2018)** – NLP Q&A platform "Warren" enhances S&P analytics  
- **SEC "RoboCop" 2013** – Accounting Quality Model flags anomalous filings for enforcement  
- **Lloyd's / FRISS Fraud Detection** – Text-mining claims boosts fraud-catch rate ≈30 %
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
**Key take-aways**

- **Alpha & Risk** – sentiment + event extraction  
- **Efficiency** – contract analysis, research Q&A  
- **Governance** – regulators spot fraud & anomalies  
- **Generative AI** – LLM-powered advisory tools
:::
